prompt:
You plan structured pruning of a language model. Answer with JSON only; do not run commands or read files.

Objective: Fit the model within the memory limit while keeping the most quality (lowest perplexity on held-out text).
Model: 28 layers, each with an MLP of 3,072 neurons and 8 key/value attention groups.
Weight memory: current 1,192.100 MB; limit 1,072.890 MB; to remove: 119.210 MB.
Current plan: all layers unpruned.

Strategies (one step each; code picks what is removed and the amount):
- narrow_mlp: delete 320 of the layer's 3,072 MLP neurons (10% of the original width), the lowest-scoring ones; frees 1.964 MB.
- remove_attention_group: delete one of the layer's 8 key/value groups (its key and value heads and the 2 query heads that share them), the lowest-scoring one; frees 1.571 MB.
- drop_layer: delete the whole layer (attention and MLP); its input passes straight to the next layer; frees 31.462 MB.
- wanda_sparsity: set a further 10% of the layer's remaining weights to zero, the lowest-scoring ones (|weight| x input size); matrices keep their shape, so it frees 0.000 MB.

Rules per candidate: each choice is one step; the same strategy on the same layer at most twice; at most 1 drop_layer, and no other choice on a dropped layer; keep at least 25% of MLP width and 1 key/value group per layer; sparsity at most 70%.
Code builds each candidate and keeps the one with the lowest perplexity, if that is at most 15% above the current plan's; later rounds continue from it.
